inputs.name: budget rule
inputs.value: sum(s_i) <= s_max; sum = n x s-bar

inputs.name: DFEs
inputs.cite: constructed test points (the post gives no example)

day.reading: the mean is the right statistic for a throughput ceiling; the DFE shape drops out
day.holds: exactly, under the Term 3 sweep time (tau proportional to 1/s): every DFE with the same sum(s_i) gives the same throughput, and sum = n x s-bar is an identity

critic.reading: each mutation has its own fixation probability; s_max is not derived
critic.holds: the cancellation needs tau proportional to 1/s (under (2/s) ln(2Ne s) the shape shifts the rate 1.4-6.8% in the test DFEs), and at a fixed mean s the shape moves the supply of fixations 1.50x (P(fix), evo007@L21). The post asserts a fixed s_max (implicit premise); it is not derived there

notes: Derivation on constructed DFEs; the post has no numeric example. The ceiling statement (given a budget, throughput is set by the budget) holds exactly under M-808's sweep time and approximately under evo005's. The critic's point concerns a different quantity: how many new mutations fix (supply), which depends on the DFE shape at a fixed mean. Whether s_max of order unity exists is H8's question (M-808, H8 q3), not settled here.
